LanguageData.Bloodfiends_TutorialText:
{PAWN_nameDef} is a Bloodfiend. {PAWN_pronoun} hungers not for food but for blood, and for the emotions that run through it.

Blood:
- Bloodfiends run on hemogen. Fresh blood feeds them best; stale sources like hemogen packs barely sate them.
- Their regeneration knits wounds and regrows limbs at the cost of hemogen, and can hold off death while there is blood to burn.

The Family:
- Every Bloodfiend belongs to a Family, ranked from First Kindred down to Lesser Kindred. Higher Kindred are stronger and command greater blood arts. See the Family tab.
- A Bloodfiend can Embrace others to make them Kindred, up to a limit. When an elder dies, everyone below them rises a generation.
- Bloodfiends of one Family share a thirst: striking your own kin weighs on the mind, striking an elder most of all.

Weaknesses:
- Bloodfiends fear deep water.
- Fire is their bane. Burns heal slowly, and a burning Bloodfiend cannot regenerate at all.

Casting will split hemogen gains in half, between the hemogen gauge and maintaining the Mantle. The Mantle requires a consistent source of hemogen to sustain itself.

LanguageData.Bloodfiends_SettingReplaceSanguophagesTi: Pawns that would be generated as sanguophages are generated as Bloodfiends instead. Vanilla's sanguophage quests no longer appear; the Bloodfiend versions take their place.
LanguageData.Bloodfiends_SettingSurviveBrainDestructi: A Bloodfiend whose brain is destroyed holds on in a mortal state and regrows it, as long as they have the hemogen. Off: brain destruction kills, as in vanilla.
LanguageData.Bloodfiends_SettingFireHindersRegenerati: Burns regenerate slowly and at a higher hemogen cost, and a burning Bloodfiend cannot regenerate at all.

LanguageData.Bloodfiends_SettingKindredSlotsFreeOnDea: Kindred slots free up when a Kindred dies
On: only living Kindred count toward the limit, so a Bloodfiend can Embrace again after losing one. Off: every Kindred a Bloodfiend ever made counts, for life.
